questions.q: Why did Ishmael and the ten men with him come to eat with Gedaliah?
Whom did Ishmael and his men kill?
questions.a: They killed Gedaliah, all the Judeans who were with him, and the Chaldean soldiers who were there.

questions.q: Who came on the second day after Ishmael had killed Gedaliah?
questions.a: Eighty men came from Shechem, Shiloh, and Samaria.
They were going to the temple.

questions.q: What did Ishmael say to the eighty men?
questions.a: He invited them to visit Gedaliah.

questions.q: What did Ishmael and his men do to the eighty men when they came into the city?
questions.a: They slaughtered the men and threw them into a pit.

questions.q: Why did they not kill ten of the eighty men?
questions.a: The ten men told them that they had provisions.

questions.q: Where did Ishmael throw the corpses of all the people he had killed?
questions.a: He threw them in the pit that King Asa had dug.

questions.q: What did Ishmael do with all the other people who were in Mizpah?
questions.a: Ishmael captured all the other people who were in Mizpah and started to take them to Ammon.

questions.q: What did Johanan and all the army commanders with him do when they heard of what Ishmael had done?
questions.a: They took all their men and went to fight against Ishmael.

questions.q: What did all the people who were with Ishmael do when they saw Johanan and all the army commanders who were with him?
questions.a: They were very happy and went to Johanan.

questions.q: Where did Ishmael and his men go to get away from Johanan?
questions.a: They went to the people of Ammon.

questions.q: Where did Johanan and the people go after they left Mizpah?
questions.a: They went to Geruth Chimham, which is near Bethlehem.

questions.q: Where did Johanan and the people want to go?
questions.a: They wanted to go to Egypt.

questions.q: Why did they want to go to Egypt?
questions.a: They were afraid of the Chaldeans.

questions.q: Why were Johanan and the people afraid of the Chaldeans?
questions.a: They were afraid because Ishmael had killed Gedaliah.

commentary.text: Ishmael murders Gedaliah. (Jer. 41:1-10) Johanan recovers the captives, and purposes to retire to Egypt. (Jer. 41:11-18)

Jer. 41:1-10 Those who hate the worshippers of God, often put on the appearance of piety, that they may the easier hurt them. As death often meets men where they least expect it, we should continually search whether we are in such a state and frame of mind, as we would wish to be found in when called to appear before our Judge. Sometimes the ransom of a man's life is his riches. But those who think to bribe death, saying, Slay us not, for we have treasures in the field, will find themselves wretchedly deceived. This melancholy history warns us, never to be secure in this world. We never can be sure of peace on this side heaven.

Jer. 41:11-18 The success of villany must be short, and none can prosper who harden their hearts against God. And those justly lose comfort in real fears, who excuse themselves in sin by pretended fears. The removal of a prudent and peaceable ruler, and the succession of another who is rash and ambitious, affects the welfare of many. Only those are happy and steady who fear the Lord and walk in his ways.
